summary.one_liner: A collection of postmortem (incident report) templates drawn from the Google SRE book, other SRE and sysadmin books, and public incident reports, plus editor setup for auto-loading them.
summary.what_it_does: ["Provides several postmortem templates, each taken from a different source: the Site Reliability Engineering book, The Practice of Cloud System Administration book, a Google Developers Blog post, Azure status history posts, Michael Kehoe's blog, the Real-World SRE book, and an Elastic Cloud incident report.", "Gives the template files under a templates/ directory, with the Site Reliability Engineering book version named as the default example in the editor instructions.", "Explains how to make Vim or Emacs insert a template automatically when you create a new file whose name starts with postmortem-.", "Lists real published incident reports as examples, such as Google Compute Engine, Azure, GitLab, Amazon DynamoDB, and Elastic Cloud.", "Includes a long list of links to articles and guides on blameless postmortems, postmortem culture, and action items."]
use_cases: Starting a new incident report after an outage
Choosing a postmortem structure for a team
Setting up Vim or Emacs to auto-fill a postmortem skeleton
Studying how companies wrote public outage reports
Finding reading material on blameless postmortem culture
how_to_run: Clone the repository into your home directory, e.g. git clone https://github.com/dastergon/postmortem-templates ~/postmortem-templates
Copy the template you want from the templates/ directory into your incident document.
Vim: add the au BufNewFile line from the README to your .vimrc, pointing at the srebook template.
Emacs: add the add-hook line from the README to your .emacs file.
Name new files postmortem-<name>-<date>.md so the auto-load pattern matches.
notable: Templates are gathered from several well-known SRE and sysadmin sources in one place.
Editor auto-load snippets for Vim and Emacs insert a template into new files named postmortem-*.
Includes links to real public incident reports to use as examples.
The resources list is broad, covering blameless culture, action items, and game-based practice such as Wheel of Misfortune.
caveats: The README does not state a license, and the templates are derived from third-party sources.
Auto-loading requires editing your own .vimrc or .emacs and cloning the repo to the path the snippets expect.
The README lists resources and examples as links only and gives no update history.
